- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and overshoot, particularly after sharp upward spikes in the history (e.g., 72.52 → 75.04 or 73.14 → 75.12).
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias: after a spike, forecasts remain high longer than actual prices, which drop sharply within 5–10 days.
- Forecasts are overly optimistic in the 10–20 day window, often ignoring recent downward momentum in the history.
- Model fails to adjust for recent low prices (e.g., 62–65 range) when they appear in the last 5–7 days of history — it still projects high values.
- Forecast error is more pronounced in the 20–30 day horizon, where model ignores short-term volatility and overweights long-term trends.
- Model underreacts to recent price drops — it doesn’t “correct” downward momentum quickly enough, leading to persistent overestimation.
- Forecasts show a lagged response to recent price changes — e.g., a 60-day drop is not reflected in 30-day forecast until 10–15 days later.
- Model tends to smooth out volatility — it doesn’t capture sudden reversals or sharp corrections in the last 5–7 days of history.
- Overconfidence in long-term trends: model assumes upward momentum continues even when recent data shows clear downward correction.
